title: Which Sierra de la Madera?
shown: The Sky Island range near Cumpas, west of the Río Bavispe.
other: Bell (2000) and Joe Hazelton's map take the Sierra de la Madera on the upper Río Bavispe, 81 km north-east.
why: From that range the wolf would reach the border without crossing the Río Bavispe, which the book has her do.

title: Where did the wolf cross the Río Bavispe?
shown: On the river's western arm, below Villa Hidalgo, within a wide circle.
other: The book names one crossing and no place.
why: The Río Bavispe is one river bent into a long U, so her way north must cross it again on the eastern arm.

title: Starvation Canyon: mouth or head?
shown: The canyon's mouth.
other: Its head, 6.4 km south-east.
why: The wolf goes to where the canyon heads and then south to Hog Canyon Spring, which is 2.4 km from the head.

title: How high between Clanton and Foster draws?
shown: The draws' mouths on the valley floor.
other: Their middle and upper reaches, about 7 km west.
why: The wolf keeps to the high ground between the draws, and the calf is killed at the head of Foster Draw.

title: The old Nations road
shown: Not on the map.
other: A crossing about a mile north of the line, near the Nations Tank on Whitewater Creek, from Bell's local informant.
why: The book names the road and nothing else about it.

title: Where was Pendleton's ranch?
shown: Not on the map.
other: About five miles north-west of Cloverdale, from Bell's local informant; Joe Hazelton's map agrees.
why: No gazetteer names the ranch.

title: Fitzpatrick Wells
shown: Not on the map.
other: The end of Fitzpatrick Camp Road, about four miles east-south-east of Cloverdale (Bell; Joe Hazelton's map).
why: The book names only the old road to the wells, and no gazetteer has them.

title: Where on Cloverdale Creek was the trap?
shown: The creek's mouth, south-east of Cloverdale.
other: Up the creek, about 7 km north-west of the town.
why: Billy turns west up the creek road from Cloverdale and rides about two hours to the trap.

title: Ciénega Springs and Government Draw
shown: Not on the map.
other: A Cienega Springs at the south end of the Animas Valley (GNIS), or north-east of Cloverdale (Bell's informant).
why: They come in an old man's story, and the sources disagree.

title: Where did Billy reach the Cajón Bonito?
shown: The stream's lower end, 47 km from Cloverdale.
other: The upper canyon, 27 km south of Cloverdale, as on Joe Hazelton's map.
why: Billy reaches the canyon a few hours after crossing the line.

title: Huisiachepic
shown: An area on the upper Río Bavispe, about 28 km south of Tamichopa.
other: No gazetteer or source has the name.
why: It may be invented or lost.

title: Where was the Parham house?
shown: At Cloverdale, with the SK Bar about 14 km north.
other: A few kilometres north of Cloverdale on the Cloverdale road, which would move the SK Bar north too.
why: Billy rides south from home and reaches Cloverdale at first light; Bell reads it the same way.

title: Old Casas Grandes or the new town?
shown: The old town, beside the Paquimé ruins.
other: Nuevo Casas Grandes, the railroad town 5 km north-east.
why: The brothers pass the ruins but ride in over the railroad and past the depot, and the only station is in the new town.

title: Which La Boquilla?
shown: La Boquilla by the lake in Gómez Farías municipio.
other: The text also calls it Boquilla y Anexas, which INEGI places 135 km away; Joe Hazelton pins one near Mata Ortiz.
why: The name is common, and the lake town fits the ride.

title: Nahuerichic
shown: Nahuerachi, 7 km south-south-west of Madera.
other: Bell independently places a Nahuerachic in about the same spot.
why: The name differs by a vowel, and nothing yet ties this town to the one in the book.

title: Which San José?
shown: San José de Ermita, 48 km north-north-west of La Boquilla.
other: Any of several San Josés in the region.
why: The name is common; this one fits the brothers' ride north up a river.

title: Soto Máynez and Santa Ana
shown: One point with Santa Ana de Babícora.
other: Two towns.
why: INEGI gives Soto Máynez as Santa Ana's official name, but the text treats them as separate places.

title: Which Álamo?
shown: An area near Galeana.
other: Joe Hazelton pins an Álamo in Sonora, 211 km away.
why: Two Álamos lie near San Buenaventura, and neither is between it and Galeana.

title: Namiquipa's direction
shown: The town of Namiquipa.
other: The text sends Billy west from Santa Ana to reach it.
why: The real town lies 25 km north-north-east of Santa Ana; the text's direction may be loose.

title: Streets and buildings in town
shown: Each town as one point.
other: Bell gives addresses: the Deming bus station, armory and cafés, the Palace Hotel and Bullard Street in Silver City, and streets in El Paso.
why: Most need a period directory or fire-insurance map to place exactly.

title: The Sierra del Nido's direction
shown: The range east-south-east of San Buenaventura.
other: The text sees it to the south.
why: The text's direction may be loose.

title: Dog Springs
shown: The border south of Hermanas.
other: Bell and Joe Hazelton put it at the Dog Mountains, 66 km away.
why: From the Dog Mountains Billy could not reach Hachita by the next evening with his travois.
